title.en: Clash query scope independent of layer visibility

summary: Confirm that hiding a layer does not change the clash result set and that every reported pair resolves to the highlighted geometry.
objective: The clash result set is identical with layers shown or hidden, and each pair carries IDs, location and an overlap measure.
applies_when: Coordination between systems or trades uses geometric intersection queries.
Layers or disciplines can be toggled while querying.
Both hard intersections and clearance violations matter.
intent_signals: hiding the duct layer hid the clash too
check the clash report against the highlighted parts
example_prompts: Check that hidden service layers still take part in clash queries.

principles: Visibility and query scope are independent; hiding a layer is a viewing action and must not silently remove elements from the clash set.
A clash result is a pair of element IDs with a location and a measured overlap, because a highlight without those values cannot be checked or fixed.
Hard clash and clearance violation are different results with different thresholds, and merging them hides the one that matters.
implementation: Define query scope explicitly as a filter over element IDs and record it with each run, keeping viewer layer visibility as a separate structure.
Author a small fixture with known answers: one true intersection, one pair separated by less than the required clearance, one pair that merely touches, and one pair inside a hidden layer.
Run the query with that layer visible and hidden, compare result sets element by element, then deduplicate symmetric pairs and confirm each appears once.
For each reported pair read the element IDs back from the highlighted objects rather than from the report, to confirm the highlight and the report agree.
observable_checks: The result set is identical with the layer shown and hidden; a difference names the code path that confused visibility with scope.

The known intersection appears as a hard clash with a nonzero overlap measure and the close pair as a clearance violation; the touching pair is assigned by the declared tolerance, and the point is that the assignment is stated rather than assumed to be zero.
Every reported pair appears exactly once, and reading IDs back from the highlighted meshes reproduces the reported pair.

known_limits: Checks the query and reporting contract; it does not establish that authored envelopes represent real equipment or that a clash-free model is buildable.
Authored verification guidance; no query was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.
